# Carve: Scenic Drive Planner

> Carve (carve.run) is a scenic-drive route planner and turn-by-turn navigation app for cars, on iPhone (with CarPlay) and Android (with Android Auto). You plan the exact roads you want, stop by stop, and Carve guides you along that route — it never swaps it for a faster one. With Carve Apex, routes download for driving with no cell signal, and Group lets everyone driving a route see each other on the map.

Carve at carve.run is separate from other apps called Carve: it is for cars, plans any route, runs on iPhone and Android, and is made by Chris Aston Chen.

- Website: https://carve.run/
- App Store (iPhone, iOS 26+): https://apps.apple.com/app/carve-route-planner/id6808087716
- Android (Android 10+): early access on Google Play; public release coming
- Made by: Chris Aston Chen
- About: https://carve.run/about/
- Contact: support@carve.run

## What it does

- Plan routes stop by stop, by search or by tapping the map; choose scenic, balanced or shortest roads
- Make a scenic loop that starts and ends where you are ("roll the dice")
- See distance, drive time and elevation before you leave
- Spoken turn-by-turn directions with live traffic, on the route you planned
- Import a route from a Google Maps link
- Share routes by link; recipients open them in Carve or any browser, and changes stay in sync
- Group: drivers on the same route see each other on the map and car screen, by name, anywhere on the route (Carve Apex; opt-in per drive, no location history)
- Made for car clubs, rallies and group drives as much as solo weekend drives

## Pricing

- Free: planning, importing, sharing, and driving with a signal
- Carve Apex: $29.99 a year with a 7-day free trial for new subscribers, or $4.99 a month. Adds offline maps and turns, Group (see your whole group on the map), 3D route previews (one free), Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and recording a drive to turn it into a route. Turn-by-turn guidance back to your route after a wrong turn (no rerouting) is free with a signal

## Famous drives
Guides to famous drives, each with a route that opens in Carve: https://carve.run/drives/

- [Skyline Boulevard](https://carve.run/drives/skyline-boulevard/): CA-35, Highway 92 to Saratoga Gap, Santa Cruz Mountains, California. Drive Skyline Boulevard (CA-35) from Highway 92 to Saratoga Gap along the crest of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Map, stops including Alice's Restaurant, and tips.
- [Big Sur, Highway 1](https://carve.run/drives/big-sur-highway-1/): CA-1, Carmel to San Simeon, Central Coast, California. Drive Big Sur on Highway 1 from Carmel to San Simeon: Bixby Bridge, McWay Falls, the elephant seals. Map, stops, current road status and tips.
- [Tioga Pass](https://carve.run/drives/tioga-pass/): Tioga Road and CA-120, Crane Flat to Lee Vining, Yosemite National Park, California. Drive Tioga Road across Yosemite from Crane Flat over 9,945-ft Tioga Pass to Lee Vining. Map, stops, opening season, fees and tips.
- [Angeles Crest Highway](https://carve.run/drives/angeles-crest-highway/): CA-2, La Cañada Flintridge to Newcomb's Ranch, San Gabriel Mountains, California. Drive the Angeles Crest Highway (CA-2) from La Cañada Flintridge to Newcomb's Ranch in the San Gabriel Mountains. Map, stops, 2026 closure status and tips.
- [Million Dollar Highway](https://carve.run/drives/million-dollar-highway/): US-550, Ouray to Silverton, San Juan Mountains, Colorado. Drive the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton: cliffside road with no guardrails over 11,018-ft Red Mountain Pass. Map, stops, season and tips.
- [Beartooth Highway](https://carve.run/drives/beartooth-highway/): US-212, Red Lodge to Cooke City, Montana and Wyoming. Drive the Beartooth Highway (US-212) from Red Lodge to Cooke City over 10,947-ft Beartooth Pass. Map, stops, opening season and tips for this All-American Road.
- [Going-to-the-Sun Road](https://carve.run/drives/going-to-the-sun-road/): West Glacier to St. Mary, Glacier National Park, Montana. Drive Going-to-the-Sun Road across Glacier National Park, from West Glacier over Logan Pass to St. Mary. Map, stops, 2026 season, vehicle limits and tips.
- [Tail of the Dragon](https://carve.run/drives/tail-of-the-dragon/): US-129 at Deals Gap, North Carolina and Tennessee. Drive the Tail of the Dragon, US-129 at Deals Gap: 318 curves in 11 miles on the North Carolina–Tennessee line. Map, stops, rules and tips.
- [Cherohala Skyway](https://carve.run/drives/cherohala-skyway/): TN-165 and NC-143, Tellico Plains to Robbinsville, Tennessee and North Carolina. Drive the Cherohala Skyway from Tellico Plains, TN to Robbinsville, NC: 15 overlooks, a crest above 5,400 feet and fall color. Map, stops, season and tips.
- [Blue Ridge Parkway](https://carve.run/drives/blue-ridge-parkway/): Mileposts 384 to 451, Asheville to Waterrock Knob, North Carolina. Drive the Blue Ridge Parkway from Asheville to Waterrock Knob, its highest section: Mount Pisgah, Graveyard Fields, Richland Balsam. Map, stops, fall color and tips.
- [Kancamagus Highway](https://carve.run/drives/kancamagus-highway/): NH-112, Lincoln to Conway, White Mountains, New Hampshire. Drive the Kancamagus Highway (NH-112) from Lincoln to Conway through the White Mountains: overlooks, waterfalls and peak fall foliage. Map, stops and tips.
- [Overseas Highway](https://carve.run/drives/overseas-highway/): US-1, Key Largo to Key West, Florida Keys. Drive the Overseas Highway (US-1) from Key Largo to Key West across 42 bridges, including the Seven Mile Bridge. Map, stops, best time to go and tips.

## Guides

- [How to plan a scenic drive](https://carve.run/plan-a-scenic-drive/): Step by step: start from a great road or describe the drive, build the route stop by stop on Scenic roads, check weather, conditions and a 3D Flyover, download it for no signal, and drive it without rerouting.
- [How to plan and lead a group drive](https://carve.run/group-drives/): Step by step for car clubs, group drives and road rallies: plan once, share one link (iPhone, Android or browser), download for no signal, turn on Group to see everyone on the map by name, brief the group, and keep it together with lead and sweep cars.

## Comparisons

How Carve compares with other apps for scenic drives, group drives, car clubs and rallies (feature charts with sources, checked October 2026): https://carve.run/compare/

- [Carve vs Google Maps](https://carve.run/compare/google-maps/): Google Maps is built to get you there fastest and reroutes on live traffic, with up to 9 stops and no driving-road library or group-drive mode. Carve keeps the exact route you planned (no rerouting), has 1,100+ hand-picked driving roads, imports Google Maps links, and with Apex adds offline turn-by-turn and Group so everyone on the route is on one map.
- [Carve vs Apple Maps](https://carve.run/compare/apple-maps/): Apple Maps has up to 14 driving stops, offline maps and CarPlay, but no scenic-road finder, no multi-stop route sharing, no Android app and no group drive. Carve finds great driving roads, never reroutes, shares one route to iPhone and Android, and with Apex adds Group so everyone is on one map.
- [Carve vs Waze](https://carve.run/compare/waze/): Waze is built to beat traffic: one stop per route, rerouting on traffic and incidents, no downloadable offline maps listed, and no group drive. Carve plans multi-stop routes on great driving roads, never reroutes, shares one route with the group, and with Apex adds offline turn-by-turn and Group live maps.
- [Carve vs REVER](https://carve.run/compare/rever/): REVER is a motorcycle-first ride app whose turn-by-turn, twisty routing, offline maps and live location are Pro ($39.99/yr), with no Android Auto. Carve is built for cars and riders alike: twisty routing, turn-by-turn and wrong-turn guidance are free, and Apex adds offline, Group live maps, CarPlay and Android Auto.
- [Carve vs Joinr](https://carve.run/compare/joinr/): Joinr is a free app for organizing car events and rally trips, with live member locations, alerts and voice messages. Carve plans the route itself — on hand-picked twisty roads — and drives it with turn-by-turn that never reroutes, offline maps, CarPlay and Android Auto, and Group so everyone sees each other on the map.
- [Carve vs ROADS by Porsche](https://carve.run/compare/roads-by-porsche/): ROADS by Porsche is a free route-finding app with a scenic route generator and community routes; drivers often report it routes them back to any waypoint they miss, and its listings don't mention offline navigation or a live group map. Carve has 1,100+ hand-picked drives, never sends you back to a skipped stop (it guides you forward to where you rejoin the route), works offline with Apex, and shows the whole group live on the map.
- [Carve vs Roadtrippers](https://carve.run/compare/roadtrippers/): Roadtrippers is a road-trip planner for places, attractions and campgrounds, with paid plans from $35.99/yr; offline maps don't give directions and it doesn't support Android Auto. Carve is for the drive itself: twisty roads, free turn-by-turn that never reroutes, offline turn-by-turn and Group live maps with Apex ($29.99/yr).
- [Carve vs Kurviger](https://carve.run/compare/kurviger/): Kurviger is a motorcycle-first curvy route planner whose navigation, offline maps and recording are on its paid Tourer+ plan; its listings don't mention a live group map. Carve has free turn-by-turn, 1,100+ hand-picked drives, and Group so everyone on a route sees each other.
